e.etymology: A modern American name in the sound family of Gavin, Evan and Aven. It has no settled source.
From Arabic salwa, comfort or consolation. The same word names the quail sent with manna to the Israelites in the Quran, a term that came from Aramaic.
A Russian and Ukrainian form of Lily, more fully Liliya, from Latin lilium.
A transposed spelling of Amelia, from the Germanic element amal, work, shared with Amalia.
e.note: Reads as a typo for Amelia, so expect it to be corrected and misspelled often.

e.etymology: A modern American spelling of Jayceon, a three-syllable name built on Jace or Jason with an -on ending. Jayceon is known as the first name of the rapper The Game.
A recent name, used mostly in Spanish-speaking families, that sets an N before Ashley, alongside Nashla and Nashly.
From the town of Cashel in County Tipperary, site of the Rock of Cashel, seat of the kings of Munster. Irish caiseal means a stone ring fort and comes from Latin castellum.
A respelling of Ryker, probably from the German and Dutch surname Riker or Rijker, from a word for rich. Ryker took off in the 2000s on the sound of Ryder and Ryan.
A respelling of Zoey with X standing for the Z sound. Zoe is Greek for life, used by early Greek-speaking Jews and Christians as a translation of Eve.
The Spanish Bible's form of Jathniel, a temple gatekeeper named in 1 Chronicles, from Hebrew Yatniel, usually read as God bestows. It is used mainly in Hispanic families.
A respelling of the surname Mabry that writes Mae into the name. Mabry is an English surname whose origin is uncertain.
A respelling of Kingsley, an English surname from a place name, Old English for the king's wood or clearing.
From Hebrew Aviyah, my father is the Lord, the name written Abijah in English Bibles and borne there by both men and women. Aviya is a modern girls' name in Israel.
A short form of Lionel or Leonardo and a spelling of Leo, all from Latin leo, lion. Lio is a nickname of soccer star Lionel Messi.
In Galician and Asturian, a short form of Anxela, Angela, from Greek angelos, messenger. Xela is also the everyday name of Quetzaltenango, Guatemala's second city, and Alex spelled backward.
A Spanish phonetic spelling of Jayden, in the way Yeison renders Jason. Jayden is a modern American name built on Jay and the -den ending.
A modern American coinage that joins West, as in Weston and Westley, to the popular -lynn ending.
A recent name in the style of Hawaiian names ending in lani, sky or heaven, close to Nalani and Noelani.
From the Book of Psalms in the Bible. Psalm comes through Latin from Greek psalmos, a song sung to a plucked string instrument. Kim Kardashian and Kanye West named a son Psalm in 2019.
The Greek god of the underworld and of the dead, brother of Zeus and Poseidon; the name is traditionally read as the unseen. It also became the word for the underworld itself.
e.note: Hades is the New Testament's word for the realm of the dead and an everyday stand-in for hell.

e.etymology: A recent American coinage in the pattern of Amari, Jamari and Omari, with the Ro- beginning of Roman and Romeo.
Hebrew Eloah, God, the singular form behind Elohim, found mostly in the Book of Job. As a girls' name it is a Brazilian fashion, usually spelled Eloa or Eloah.
e.note: Eloah is a Hebrew name for God, which some religious families may find unsuitable for a child.

e.etymology: From an English surname that goes back to the Old English woman's name Wilburg, from wil, will, and burh, fortress. It was a popular American first name from the 1880s to the 1930s.

assoc.t: the pig saved by a spider in Charlotte's Web

e.meaning: ruler of the home (Henry) or army leader (Harold)
e.etymology: A medieval English pet form of Harry, itself the everyday form of Henry, with r turned to l as in Sally from Sarah. Shakespeare's Prince Hal is the young Henry V. It also serves for Harold.
namesakes: Hal Holbrook (actor famous for playing Mark Twain)

assoc.t: HAL 9000, rogue computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey

e.etymology: A spelling of Roderick, from a Germanic name meaning famous ruler, the same name as Spanish Rodrigo. Roderick was revived after Walter Scott used it in an 1811 poem.
namesakes: Rodrick Heffley (Greg's older brother in Diary of a Wimpy Kid)

assoc.t: Rodrick Heffley, big brother in Diary of a Wimpy Kid

e.meaning: he who holds firm the good
e.etymology: An African American coinage that sets the La- prefix before Darius, the Persian royal name meaning he who holds firm the good.
The Spanish form of Latin Horatius, a Roman family name of obscure origin, borne by the poet Horace. Horatio is the related English form.
A pet form of names beginning with Elv-, chiefly Elvira and Elva for girls and Elvin for boys. It was in use across the US around 1900.
From the surname Neely, a short form of McNeely, Gaelic for son of the poet. As a girls' name it followed Neely O'Hara, a lead character of the 1966 novel Valley of the Dolls.
A spelling of Talon, the English word for a bird of prey's claw, reshaped in the mold of Jalen and Kalen.

A Scottish clan surname of Norman origin, a contraction of Saint Clair, from a place in Normandy named for a saint whose Latin name means bright or clear. Novelist Sinclair Lewis made it familiar as a first name.
namesakes: Sinclair Lewis (Nobel Prize-winning novelist of Main Street and Babbitt)

assoc.t: Sinclair gas stations with the green dinosaur logo

e.etymology: From Arabic nasir, one who helps or grants victory, the active participle of nasara, to aid. Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser made the name known worldwide.
namesakes: Gamal Abdel Nasser (president of Egypt, 1956 to 1970)
